0.label: top_rim_face_and_crocodiles
0.description: The whole top edge of the drawn tray: a face shown by two large lashed eyes and a faint nose and mouth at the centre, a hatched crocodile to its left and a lozenge-marked block with a ribbed reptile to its right.
0.iconography: The ojú ọpọ́n (Ẹ̀ṣù) face flanked by crocodiles — the messenger between the water's dangerous powers. A band, not one motif.

1.label: left_rim_animal_file
1.description: The left edge: a crocodile, a tortoise, a round shell-like creature, a quadruped marked with a lozenge and a ribbed reptile, stacked top to bottom.
1.iconography: A file of water and earth creatures — crocodile, tortoise (Ìjàpá) — the animals of offering and danger that ring Ifá's field.

2.label: right_rim_animal_file
2.description: The right edge: crocodiles or lizards with ribbed bodies, skeletal fish forms and a quadruped, stacked top to bottom — the counterpart of #1.
2.iconography: The mirror file of creatures; fish and crocodiles make the right side the watery one.

panel.title: Survey drawing of a rectangular Ifá tray (35 × 41 cm): a border of crocodiles, fish and tortoises
panel.object_type: pen-and-ink survey drawing of a rectangular opon Ifá
panel.summary: A drawing captioned 'Ifabrett, 35 × 41 cm, Yoruba 3' of a rectangular tray whose border is almost entirely animals: crocodiles, lizards, fish and tortoises, with a face shown by two large eyes at the top centre.

register_readings.reading: Top: the face (eyes, nose, mouth) between a crocodile and a ribbed reptile.
Sides: files of crocodiles, tortoises, fish and quadrupeds.
Foot (undetected): a toothed crocodile with a curled tail, a chevron-filled oval (fish or bundle), and a tortoise seen from above.

panel.composition: A frame of animals facing along the rim, sides roughly mirrored, with the face as the single frontal element.
panel.narrative: A tray devoted to the creatures of river and bush — above all the crocodile, repeated around the frame. Read with the knotted serpents of KBA_10298 and the crocodile of FoA_04-5586, it shows how often Ifá's field is ringed by the dangerous water powers (Olókun's realm) that offerings keep in balance.
cross_panel_links: Same caption formula as KBA_10299, KBA_15356.
uncertainties: The three boxes are whole sides of the frame, not motifs; the bottom side is missed.
